content: Yaws is a tropical infectious disease that primarily affects the skin, bones, and joints. It is caused by the spirochete bacterium Treponema pertenue. Other diseases caused by related treponemal bacteria include bejel (Treponema endemicum), pinta (Treponema carateum), syphilis (Treponema pallidum), and Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi). Yaws is specifically caused by the spiral-shaped bacterium Treponema pallidum subspecies pertenue. While it is closely related to the bacterium responsible for syphilis, yaws is not transmitted through sexual contact. To diagnose yaws, a sample from a skin lesion is examined using a specialized microscope technique called darkfield microscopy. There is no specific blood test available for yaws. However, blood tests for syphilis often yield positive results in individuals with yaws due to the close relationship between the bacteria causing these two conditions. Treatment for yaws typically involves a single dose of a specific type of penicillin. For cases in the later stages of the disease, three weekly doses of penicillin are administered. Recurrence of the disease is rare following treatment. It is recommended that all individuals living in the same household as an infected person undergo examination for yaws and receive treatment if they are found to be infected.
